newsitem.title: KENYA: RALLYING-MCRAE SURVIVES SCARE TO LEAD SAFARI RALLY.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE SURVIVES SCARE TO LEAD SAFARI RALLY.

text.p: Briton Colin McRae narrowly stayed out of trouble on the second day of the Safari Rally to open up a slight lead over compatriot Richard Burns and set himself up for a first victory of the season.

The Subaru driver, who has only claimed one fourth place finish in the two rounds of the championship so far this season, set the fastest time on four of the second day's five stages to lead by more six minutes over his Mitsubishi rival.
But McRae had to endure a frightening moment on the fifth stage when spectators tried to sabotage his car by placing rocks along the road.

"There was a one foot high wall of stones and we hit it flat out," said the Subaru driver. "The car jumped in the air and I thought we had taken the whole front end off the car. Luckily, we just damaged one corner very badly."
Second-placed Burns seemed to be on a charge at the end of the day as he closed the gap on McRae, despite clipping a goat on the day's eighth stage.
Kenya's Ian Duncan, the local favourite who briefly led the rally after the opening stage of the event, was left complaining of a slightly overheating engine and shock absorber problems.
"We're playing safe and driving around the things that do the damage," he said.
A victory for McRae after Monday's final four stages would give him the lead in the world championship over Carlos Sainz, who retired on the opening day.
Reigning world champion Finn Tommi Makinen added his name to the casualty list on Sunday when he sustained three punctures on the fifth stage and was forced to stop his Mitsubishi.
The final leg of the rally on Monday sees the teams head south of Nairobi to the same punishing route which caught out many of the drivers on Saturday.
